title: High Spatial Resolution MALDI IMS Data Acquisition for Metabolites in Negative Ion Mode
author: Ali Zahraei
materials: Use FlexImaging software to load the optical image of the slides. Define the target position using three teaching points. Verify teaching accuracy by moving the stage to a fourth reference location and confirming accurate alignment between the stage position and optical image.

steps.title: Prepare instrument and parameters
steps.instruction: Load the MTP slide adapter 2 into the instrument, open timsControl software, select the appropriate MALDI IMS data acquisition method, and measure the target height at multiple locations across the slide, confirming that height variation is less than 10 µm.

substeps.instruction: Load MTP slide adapter 2 into the instrument.
Select the appropriate MALDI IMS data acquisition method.
Measure target height at several points on the slide.

steps.title: Set acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the acquisition for 10 µm spatial resolution with the following settings: m/z range 50–900, laser power 50–60 %, laser frequency 10,000 Hz, 100–200 laser shots per pixel, 10 µm spot size (beam scanning disabled), and source temperature 50 °C.

steps.title: Perform external TOF calibration
steps.instruction: Run an external TOF calibration using red phosphorus, confirm that all calibration points meet the 99 % acceptance criterion, and abort data acquisition if the criterion is not met. (Alternative: use Agilent ESI‑L LCMS Tuning Solution when operating in ESI mode.)

substeps.instruction: Perform external TOF calibration with red phosphorus.
Confirm each calibration point meets ≥ 99 % acceptance.
If acceptance < 99 %, do not proceed with data acquisition.

steps.title: Define ROI and start acquisition
steps.instruction: Create a region of interest (ROI) in FlexImaging software that matches the tissue boundaries and desired pixel/raster size, verify correct placement, and then start data acquisition within FlexImaging.

substeps.instruction: Confirm ROI aligns with tissue boundaries and pixel/raster size.
